newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NEW ARRIVAL SCORES LAST GASP GOAL FOR WHALER VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NEW ARRIVAL SCORES LAST GASP GOAL FOR WHALER VICTORY.

text.p: New arrival Curtis Leschyshyn scored with 4.6 seconds left in overtime in his first game as a Whaler, giving Hartford a 4-3 triumph on Saturday over the slumping Buffalo Sabres.
Leschyshyn was acquired before the game from Washington for forward Andrei Nikolishin and made it to Hartford less than an hour before the opening faceoff.

Geoff Sanderson, who scored twice, started the final play when he shrugged off an Alexei Zhitnik check and threaded a pass into the low slot. Leschyshyn snuck in from the blue line and wristed the puck over goalie Dominik Hasek's shoulder.
"I couldn't have scripted this game any better," he said.
Hartford coach Paul Maurice said: "It was a great heads up play by Leschyshyn. He knew how much time was left and knew it would do no good to stay back at the blue line."
Hartford won for the second time in eight games (2-3-3), despite a 40-save performance by Hasek for the Sabres, winless in five of their last six games (1-4-1).
At Florida, Scott Mellanby and Johan Garpenlov each had a goal and an assist to lead the high-riding Florida Panthers to a 4-2 victory over the homesick Pittsburgh Penguins.
Florida star goaltender John Vanbiesbrouck suffered a leg injury with 2:06 to go in the first period and was replaced by Mark Fitzpatrick, but the Panthers didn't miss a beat.
"It was probably the best thing that happened," Vanbiesbrouk said. "Mark came in and did a terrific job."
Fitzpatrick recorded 22 saves to improve to 3-0-1 on the season. "Having two great goaltenders is a luxury most team's don't have," said Mellanby. The Panthers improved to 10-1-4.
The Penguins (4-10-1) again failed to post their first road win of the season and fell to 0-9-1 away from home.
It was the first meeting between the teams since the Eastern Conference Finals last season when Florida rebounded from a one-game deficit to beat Pittsburgh in seven games.
Penguins star Mario Lemieux sat out because of a bad back.
At Washington, Todd Krygier's goal with 58 seconds left snapped a tie and lifted the Washington Capitals to a 3-2 victory over the New York Rangers.
Washington is 5-2-1 in its last eight games against New York. The Rangers are 0-2-1 in their last three overall.

Joe Juneau, who assisted on all three goals, picked up the puck in the neutral zone. He laid a behind-the-back backhand pass on the stick of Krygier, whose wrist shot from the high slot beat Glenn Healy at 19:02.
In Calgary, Brett Hull's power-play goal with 3:51 left in the third period gave the St Louis Blues a 3-2 victory over the Calgary Flames, who suffered their fourth straight loss.
Hull, who began his career with the Flames in 1985, was in the slot when he one-timed a Geoff Courtnall feed past goaltender Rick Tabaracci, who had lost his stick.
"We moved the puck well and then Geoff gave me a great pass and I just got it away as quick as I could," said Hull.
Grant Fuhr made 27 saves for the Blues, including 17 in the third period.

At Colorado, Scott Young recorded his third career hat trick and goalie Patrick Roy defeated his former team for the second time in as many starts as the Colorado Avalanche rolled to a 5-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.
Young opened the scoring at 6:04 of the first period with a power-play marker and put the Avalanche ahead again 2-1 with his eighth goal of the season with 2:25 left in the period.
Young added another power-play tally in the final minute of the second period as Colorado (11-4) extended their unbeaten streak to nine games.

In Toronto, Wendel Clark recorded his second career four-goal game, including a natural hat trick in the second period as the Toronto Maple Leafs routed the Edmonton Oilers 7-3 for their seventh win in nine games.
"The bounces were going right," said Clark. "It was opportunistic. The shots went in. Whenever you have a big game, you can narrow it down to team play."
In Ottawa, Adam Oates and Jean Yves-Roy scored third-period goals and the Boston Bruins stayed unbeaten in 22 games against the Ottawa Senators by rallying for a 4-3 win.
Rookie Yevgeny Shaldybin and Bob Beers also scored for Boston, 20-0-2 against the Senators since they entered the NHL in 1992-93.
Oates lifted Boston into a 3-3 tie with 9:52 left in regulation and Roy scored the game-winner with 5:42 left.

At New Jersey, Martin Brodeur combined with Mike Dunham on New Jersey's second shutout in four days and Petr Sykora and Bill Guerin each had a goal and an assist as the Devils beat the New York Islanders 4-0 for their fourth straight win.

Brodeur, playing all but 40 seconds in the third period, turned aside all 19 shots. Dunham was inserted with 11:45 remaining so he can play in 24 games and avoid becoming a free agent at the end of the season. He faced no shots.

In Philadelphia, Gary Suter and Tony Amonte each had a goal and an assist and Jeff Hackett made 33 saves as the Chicago Blackhawks beat the Flyers 4-1 for their first win in Philadelphia in more than six years.
Chicago broke the skid in Philadelphia's new CoreStates Centre behind Hackett, who made eight saves in the first period, 16 in the second and nine in the third.
